referenceSystemInfo.name: NZGD2000 / NZCS2000 (New Zealand Continental Shelf 2000)
referenceSystemInfo.note: The reference system of the published output. NZCS2000 is a Lambert Conformal Conic projection covering New Zealand's full offshore continental shelf, chosen over NZTM2000 (EPSG:2193) because it suits an extent spanning the antimeridian, including the outlying islands.

referenceSystemInfo.name: WGS 84
referenceSystemInfo.note: The working reference system: the classification is indexed to the H3 discrete global grid system, which operates in WGS84 lat/lon. Also used for the geographic bounding box recorded in this metadata's extent.

referenceSystemInfo.name: NZGD2000 / New Zealand Transverse Mercator 2000 (NZTM2000)
referenceSystemInfo.note: Used elsewhere within the wider LUIS project (other classifications with mainland-only extents) for metric (area/distance) calculations; not used for this output, noted here for completeness only.

dggs.system: H3 (Uber H3 hexagonal discrete global grid system)
dggs.note: The classification is performed per H3 cell at resolution 11, then dissolved into the multipolygon features that make up the published output.

identificationInfo.abstract: NZLUM (New Zealand Land Use and Management classification) is a national land use and management dataset for New Zealand, produced by combinatorial classification of many authoritative spatial datasets aligned to a discrete global grid system (DGGS), using the Land Use Information System (LUIS). Each location is independently assessed against a three-tier hierarchy of land use classes (primary/secondary/tertiary codes) defined by the NZSLUC classification system: 1 = Conservation and natural environments (e.g. nature conservation, cultural and natural heritage, minimal-use natural environments including defence land, unused/transitioning land); 2 = Production land uses (e.g. plantation forestry, dairy and dry stock grazing, cropping, horticulture, intensive animal production, water/wastewater, smallholder farms); 3 = Built environments (e.g. residential density tiers, recreation and community services, commercial, manufacturing and industrial, utilities, transportation, mining, waste treatment). Alongside the class identification, each unit carries a confidence score, spatial scale, and source date range describing the evidentiary basis of its classification.
identificationInfo.purpose: To provide a single, nationally consistent land use and management classification for New Zealand's territorial sea extent, resolving many overlapping and variably-scaled authoritative datasets (national topographic, cadastral, land-cover, and land-use datasets; and regional council resource-consent, hazard, and land-use datasets) into one dataset with a common schema, suitable for national-scale land use analysis, reporting, and planning.

pointOfContact.positionName: Senior Researcher – Geospatial and Remote Sensing

resourceMaintenance.note: Regenerated as contributing input datasets or classification rules change. Further versions are expected as the NZSLUC classification system and its contributing datasets evolve.

descriptiveKeywords.note: The 18 place names after 'New Zealand territorial sea' are the regional layer names the published dataset is split into, covering all regional/unitary authority areas plus two catch-all layers for area outside any region and the outlying islands.

spatialResolution.note: Average H3 resolution-11 hexagon edge length. Individual contributing input datasets vary considerably in native scale/resolution.

geographicElement.note: Bounding rectangle only, crossing the antimeridian (180°) to include the Kermadec Islands to the northeast. Taken from the published dataset's own extent. The true footprint is the New Zealand 12 nautical mile territorial sea polygon - mainland New Zealand plus outlying island groups (Kermadec, Chatham, Auckland, Campbell, Antipodes, Bounty, Snares) - not a filled rectangle.

temporalElement.note: No single production/observation date applies: the dataset is a composite of contributing source datasets with their own source date ranges, spanning at least 1973 to the present across known contributing sources.

useConstraints.note: Confirmed as the license recorded by the publisher on the LRIS Portal.

resourceConstraints.otherConstraints: Some contributing input datasets carry restricted-use terms - notably two District Valuation Roll (DVR) derived layers used under permission from the Ministry for the Environment (MfE). The published output does not expose the restricted source geometries or attributes directly; it carries only derived/aggregated classification values (land use class, confidence, source metadata) at the resolution of the H3 grid. Users with questions about a specific contributing dataset's terms should contact the point of contact for this record.

attributes.name: unit_id
attributes.description: A deterministic hash of a subset of the unit's own classification attributes (used to identify/dissolve H3 cells sharing the same classification result). Used as the GeoPackage feature id, but is not a persistently-assigned or guaranteed-unique per-feature identifier, and is not stable across reclassification runs if the hashed attributes change.

attributes.name: lu_code_primary
attributes.description: Primary (top-level, 1 digit) NZSLUC land use code, e.g. 1 = Conservation and natural environments, 2 = Production land uses, 3 = Built environments.

attributes.name: lu_code_secondary
attributes.description: Secondary (second-level) NZSLUC land use code, refining the primary code.

attributes.name: lu_code_tertiary
attributes.description: Tertiary (third-level, most specific) NZSLUC land use code, refining the secondary code.

attributes.name: lu_code
attributes.description: Dotted concatenation of the primary, secondary, and tertiary codes (e.g. '1.3.6').

attributes.name: lu_description
attributes.description: Human-readable label for the lu_code, derived from the NZSLUC v0.4.0 classification system definition.

attributes.name: lu_code_ancillary
attributes.description: Additional/ancillary land use code(s) applicable to the same unit, where more than one use co-occurs.

attributes.name: commod
attributes.description: Commodity or commodities associated with the classified use (e.g. specific crop or livestock types), where known.

attributes.name: manage
attributes.description: Management practice(s) associated with the classified use (e.g. crop-pasture rotation, irrigation type), where known.

attributes.name: land_estate
attributes.description: Estate/tenure type of the underlying property title (from LINZ District Valuation Roll / Records of Title), where available.

attributes.name: land_status
attributes.description: Land governance/management status (e.g. Crown, local authority, private), derived primarily from the Central Record of State Land (CRoSL) and District Valuation Roll.

attributes.name: water
attributes.description: Water feature type intersecting or coincident with the unit (e.g. river, lake, lagoon, swamp, mangrove), where applicable.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.description: Planning zone category (e.g. Rural, Residential, Industrial, Commercial, Recreational), derived from District Valuation Roll zone codes.

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.description: Relative confidence in the classification of this unit (lower value = higher confidence), used to prioritise between competing candidate classifications during processing.

attributes.name: luc_date
attributes.description: Date on which this unit was processed/classified by the LUIS workflow.

attributes.name: source_data
attributes.description: Name(s) of the contributing source dataset(s) that determined this unit's classification.

attributes.name: source_date
attributes.description: Date range over which the contributing source data is valid/current.

attributes.name: source_scale
attributes.description: Spatial scale/precision range (in metres) of the contributing source data.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.description: Free-text remarks; reserved for classification-specific notes.

lineage.statement: NZLUM is produced by the Land Use Information System (LUIS), which partitions New Zealand's territorial sea extent into H3 discrete global grid cells at resolution 11, then evaluates each cell independently against a series of per-class rules drawing on a large and evolving set of authoritative input datasets. Where more than one candidate classification applies to a cell, rules prefer the more confident, more recent, and more spatially precise identification. Contributing input dataset categories include: Toitu Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand (LINZ) topographic, cadastral, and property/title datasets; Manaaki Whenua - Landcare Research datasets including the Land Cover Database (LCDB) and NZ Land Resource Inventory Land Use Capability (NZLRI LUC); Ministry for the Environment (MfE) and Statistics New Zealand (Stats NZ) datasets; Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) marine farm data; and regional council resource-consent, contaminated-land (HAIL), land-categorisation, and land-use survey datasets from a wide range of regional and unitary authorities. The full, current list of contributing datasets changes as datasets are added and is intentionally not duplicated verbatim in this metadata record.
